audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phases[N].side read 'Skill' while content win[0..6] read Lux, Lux, Galio, Galio, Galio, Lux, Galio — the page rendered two answers for every stage.
audit.why: Lux out-ranges Galio at every level (Q 1175, E 1100, W 1150 against Q 825 and E 650), so she owns levels 1-2 and the first-item window; Galio owns 3 through 6, when Justice Punch and Hero's Entrance make the gap crossable. That is what the content layer and packet.levelChart already said.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes named only Galio spikes and no Lux spike, contradicting a chart that hands her the first-item row.
audit.why: Her first item raises poke damage and the Final Spark execute threshold — Final Spark is 60s at rank 1 falling to 40s, reaching 3340. That is the row she wins.
audit.corrected: breakdown.spikes and phases[5].why now name it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page asserted 'minion-block it' with no grounding and never mentioned Illumination's mechanic. Light Binding binds up to two enemy units, so it stops on a minion line; Illumination only cashes out when Lux lands a basic attack.
audit.why: Riot Q text: 'binds and deals damage to up to two enemy units.' Riot passive text: 'Lux's next attack ignites the energy, dealing bonus magic damage.' Both change how a Galio stands in lane and neither was stated with its source.
audit.corrected: Grounded in winCon, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.early, breakdown.wave, dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[0].d.
sources: kit: Lux P and Q text

audit.why: Light Binding is a flat 10s at every rank — it never gets shorter, which makes it the single most reliable commit window in the lane and is exactly the sort of fact the field exists to carry.
audit.corrected: Rewrote with Light Binding 10s flat, Lucent Singularity 10s to 8s at 1100, Final Spark 60s to 40s.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet flagged 'Your Hero's Entrance' in spikes[1].
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is Galio's real R. False positive; no change made.

edits.before: Lux wins by landing Light Binding, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.

edits.before: Ahead, tax both maps: zone Lux with taunt threat, keep the wave middle, and R every skirmish — fed Galio makes the enemy jungler unemployed.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-cleared middle wave that keeps your R timer flexible — Galio waves are about being free to leave. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.

Worst wave: a wave shoved to her tower, where a 1175-range Q and an 1100-range E cover the whole approach. Crash timing: crash after her Q is spent, so the ten seconds it costs her are the ten you use to leave.
